steps.name: QC and DESeq2 differential expression, treated vs control
caveats: This is a 3' tag-seq library (one read per transcript 3' end) — do not apply gene-length normalization (TPM/FPKM) at any point; DESeq2 raw-count median-of-ratios normalization is appropriate as-is
n=3 per group is small; treat nominal p-values with caution and rely on the BH-adjusted p-value and shrunken fold changes for ranking, not raw p-value alone
Single batch, unpaired design — no batch correction or paired-test structure is needed or should be introduced
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=3) and control (n=3) liver samples in this raw gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 6 samples) from a Lexogen QuantSeq 3' FWD tag-seq library?
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix (12000 x 6) and 6-sample metadata are loaded and sample IDs are matched/ordered identically between the two files
Genes with near-zero counts across all samples are filtered before modeling (e.g. require count >= 10 in at least 3 samples) and the number of genes retained after filtering is reported

DESeq2 is run with design ~ condition (treated vs control) on raw integer counts with default median-of-ratios size-factor normalization — no length-based normalization (TPM/FPKM/RPKM) is applied at any stage, consistent with this being a 3' tag-seq library

Log2 fold changes are shrunk with apeglm (or ashr if apeglm coefficient naming fails) and results table includes baseMean, log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value for every tested gene
A full results table (all genes) and a filtered significant-gene table (padj < 0.05) are written out, plus a PCA plot and an MA plot / volcano plot for QC and reporting
Sample-level QC (library size per sample, PCA or sample-sample correlation) is reported to flag any outlier sample before interpreting the DE result

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on DE results
caveats: WikiPathways human GMT here uses HGNC gene symbols with a '%'-delimited descriptor field that must be split to recover a readable pathway name before reporting results
With only 12000 genes profiled and a small sample size, enrichment results should be treated as hypothesis-generating, not confirmatory
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human biological pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
acceptance_criteria: A ranked gene list (by shrunken log2FoldChange or by DESeq2 test statistic, from T1S1's full results table) is used to run pre-ranked GSEA against WikiPathways human gene sets, and a separate over-representation test is run on the padj<0.05 significant gene set from T1S1 against the same pathway collection
Gene symbols in the DE results are matched to the WikiPathways human GMT's HGNC symbol space directly (both are human gene symbols) without needing external ID mapping

Output includes a table of enriched pathways with normalized enrichment score (GSEA) or odds ratio/adjusted p-value (ORA), sorted by significance, and reports how many DE genes matched the pathway gene universe
If fewer than ~10 genes pass padj<0.05, this is stated explicitly and the GSEA pre-ranked result (which uses all genes, not just significant ones) is reported as the primary enrichment result

plan.title: 3' tag-seq DESeq2 DE: treated vs control liver
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a small (12,000 gene x 6 sample) raw-count matrix from a Lexogen QuantSeq 3' FWD tag-seq run of human liver samples, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. Because QuantSeq is a 3' tag-seq protocol (one read per transcript molecule, no gene-length dependence), standard length-based normalizations (TPM/FPKM) are inappropriate and must not be used; DESeq2's median-of-ratios normalization operating directly on raw gene counts is the correct approach and requires no gene-length correction step. With only 3 vs 3 replicates, effect-size shrinkage (apeglm/ashr) is used to stabilize log2FC estimates against the high variance expected at this n. The plan is: (1) QC and low-count filtering of the raw matrix, (2) DESeq2 differential expression with condition as the sole factor (single batch, no covariates needed) and shrunken log fold changes, (3) pathway enrichment (GSEA-style and/or over-representation) on the resulting ranked gene list using WikiPathways human gene sets confirmed present in the reference store. No immune, PK/PD, safety, or multi-omics considerations apply — the research question is a straightforward two-group DE comparison with a downstream biological-interpretation layer.
